envelope.text: or `nullptr` when @p policy is not exactly one policy bit.

why:
RE-VERDICTED gap -> divergence, phase-417 G6/G7 — WE HAVE IT NOW, and the shape differs for a platform reason. `nros::qos_policy_kind_to_cstr(uint32_t)` (`packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/qos.hpp`) forwards to `rclc_qos_policy_kind_to_cstr`, which forwards to `nros_rmw::QoSPolicyMask::policy_name_cstr` — one table, three surfaces, no copy.

TWO DIFFERENCES, both from the vocabulary rather than from taste. (1) The PARAMETER: upstream takes `const rclcpp::QosPolicyKind&`, an enum whose enumerators are a second naming of the same policies. Ours takes the MASK BIT, because the bitmask is the vocabulary this tree already has in two languages — `QoSPolicyMask`'s twelve consts and `NROS_RMW_QOS_POLICY_*` in `rmw_entity.h`, held equal name for name and bit for bit by `check-qos-mask-derivation` R0 — and it is what a backend advertises through the vtable's `supported_qos_policies` slot. A thirteenth enum would be the parallel table this row exists to prevent. (2) The INVALID answer: upstream returns `"Invalid"` for its invalid enumerator; we return `nullptr` for the empty mask and for a union, because a caller must be able to tell 'no policy was identified' from a policy that was — a refusal relayed from a C backend crosses `rmw_ret_t`, which has no room for a mask.

WHAT IT IS FOR, which is the part the original row got right: `QoSProfile::validate_against` computed the offending policy and returned a bare `TransportError::IncompatibleQos`, while `rmw_vtable.h`'s `supported_qos_policies` block told the reader those creates fail 'naming a policy' — the argument issue 1329 used for choosing NONE over the union. G7 made it true: the error carries the bit, `nros-node`'s `validate_qos_or_report` logs the name at all eleven create sites, and the zenoh shim's own refusals now name the policy instead of a hand-written lowercase field word.
